video.title: isCancelled, checkCancellation & withTaskCancellationHandler | Day 274
video.description:
Learn to explain how to say that a task should stop, check for a stop request and clean up when it is cancelled: isCancelled, checkCancellation & withTaskCancellationHandler, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
isCancelled - A task property that is true once someone has asked the task to stop.
checkCancellation - A call that throws an error when the current task was cancelled, so the work stops early.
withTaskCancellationHandler - A function that runs your cleanup closure right away when the surrounding task is cancelled.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain isCancelled, checkCancellation and withTaskCancellationHandler in English?

dialogue.title: The download that never stops
dialogue.setting: Fixing a task that ignores cancellation

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, users leave the screen, but my download keeps going.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cancel the task. Cancellation is cooperative, so your code must look for it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do I look for it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Read isCancelled. It is true once someone has asked the task to stop.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And if I want to stop with an error?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Call checkCancellation. It throws when the task was cancelled.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use withTaskCancellationHandler. Its `onCancel` closure runs right away on cancel.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Even while the task is waiting?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. isCancelled only helps when you look at it. The handler fires by itself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So withTaskCancellationHandler for cleanup, and checkCancellation to stop early.
Check isCancelled inside the long loop.
